blocks.text: **Tabulation** builds the DP answer **bottom-up**: make a table with one cell per subproblem, fill in the base cases, then fill every other cell **in an order where everything it depends on is already filled**. No recursion, no call stack — just loops. When the last cell is filled, it holds the answer.

blocks.alt: The table of C(i, j), the number of ways to choose j items from i, for i up to 5 and j up to 3. Column 0 is all 1s. Every other cell is the sum of the cell diagonally above-left and the cell directly above: C(5, 2) = C(4, 1) + C(4, 2) = 4 + 6 = 10. Filling row by row, left to right, guarantees both are ready.

blocks.text: How to turn a recursion into a table

items: **The table's shape is the state**: one dimension per changing argument. fib(n) → a 1D array of n + 1 cells; C(i, j) → a 2D table.
**Base cases go in first**: the cells the recurrence can't compute from others.
**The recurrence becomes the loop body**: `dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j−1] + dp[i−1][j]` reads two cells and writes one.
**Choose the loop order from the dependencies**: every cell a cell reads must come earlier in the loops.

blocks.caption: Each cell is filled from the two cells above it, row by row.

blocks.text: **Time O(n · k), space O(n · k).** The recurrence is **Pascal's rule**: to choose j of the first i items, either item i is chosen (and j − 1 come from the rest) or it isn't (and all j do).
Choosing the order: follow the arrows
Draw an arrow from every cell a cell **reads** to the cell itself. Any order that fills cells after everything pointing into them works. The common shapes:

blocks.code:
dp[i] reads dp[i-1], dp[i-2]              left to right        (Fibonacci, Climbing Stairs, House Robber)
dp[i] reads dp[i+1], dp[i+2]              right to left        (suffix problems, Decode Ways backwards)
dp[r][c] reads above and to the left      row by row           (grid paths, LCS, edit distance)
dp[l][r] reads shorter ranges inside      by increasing length  (palindromes, burst balloons)
dp[amount] reads smaller amounts          amount 0, 1, 2, ...   (coin change)

blocks.text: Fibonacci, for example, is a 1D table filled left to right:

blocks.alt: Memoization (top-down): O(states) time, O(states) + stack space. Tabulation (bottom-up): O(states) time, O(states) space.

items: **Memoization** is quicker to write from a recursion and computes **only the states it needs** — good when many states are never reached.
**Tabulation** has **no recursion** (no stack overflow, less overhead), and its regular loops make the next trick — saving memory — possible.
Both have the same time complexity. In interviews, write whichever you can get right; mention the other.
A table cell per state; base cases first; the recurrence is the loop body.
Fill in an order where every cell's dependencies are already filled.
Row by row for grids and two strings, by length for intervals, by amount for coin problems.
Same time as memoization, no call stack.
